text.p: These are the leading stories in the Serbian and Montenegrin press on Friday. Reuters has not verified them nor does it vouch for their accuracy.
-- SERBIA
POLITIKA

- Serbian President Slobodan Milosevic received U.N. administratior for Eastern Slavonia in Croatia and Serb leadership in the region. The issue of dual citizenship for the citizens of the region will be resolved through bilateral agreement between Croatia and Federal Republic of Yugoslavia.
- Federal parliament re-elected Radoje Kontic as a prime minister. It also ratified the Agreement on special and parallel relations between Yugoslavia and Bosnian Serbs.
- Serbian Prime Minister Mirko Marjanovic said republic's draft law on privatisation will be presented to reporters on Monday.
- Serbian power industry will not on April 1 return prices of electricity to summer tariff, 33 percent lower than during winter.
- The Association of Serbian trade unions says new law on ownership tansformation is acceptable as it promises relatively quick, just and controled privatisation.

- Serbian minister for economic and ownership transformation Milan Beko said the privatisation bill was comprehensively reformist and just and that it respects the principle of openness in its enactment and implementation.
- The Association of Yugoslav Banks agree interest rates must be cut but only if induced by market forces.
- Belgrade city council revokes three percent city tax.
NASA BORBA

- Yugoslav Prime Minister Radoje Kontic said four strategic aims of the government are modern, democratic, social and state of law, reintegration in interantional community, open market economy and raise in standard of living and citizens' social security.
- Belgrade students ended protest after 119 days.
- Milan Panic, former Yugoslav Prime Minister, said he would accept to run for presidental elections in Serbia as a candidate of opposition and some socialists.
- Serbia's bill on consessions should be outlined by the end of next week.
- The group of 17 economists said restitution followed with mass voucher privatisation could get Serbia closer to Czech model of privatisation.
- Radovan Kovacevic, director of the Foreign Trade Institute said said governemnt must break monopolies in foreign trade.

- Serbian-Chinese barter deal between Belgrade Jugopetrol and China Sinochem extended till 2002. Some 10 million tonnes of crude should be imported to Yugoslavia in the next five years. Details of the deal a secret.
- Belgrade chain of department stores Robna kuca Beograd faces receivership. Bankruptcy case before the Higher Economic Court. Proposal for the banks to take over the entire business.

- Crown Prince Aleksandar Karadjordjevic appeals on leading politicians to put the interest of people and country above party or personal interests. Future of Serbia's and Montenegrin relations depends on establishment of democracy.

- BK television says that as of Thursday evening they are not allowed to use Avala-Jastrebac television transmitter so the programme of this private TV station cannot be received in Jagodina, Aleksinac, Nis, Leskovac, Kragujevac, Paracin, Cuprija, Batocina and Lapovo.
MONTENEGRO
POBJEDA

- The programme of the new Yugoslav government reflects main goals of the (ruling Montenegrin) Democratic Party of Socialists, said Zeljko Sturanovic, head of the party's club of federal parliament members.

- Montenegrin government appeals to all media in the republic not to accept the media war initiated by a part of Belgrade press but to be guided by civilisation standards of free press in the interest of stable relations in the common state of Yugoslavia.

- Montenegro's foreign policy priorities are to continue and intensify co-operation with the United States and to have an active role in negotiations with the International Monetary Fund and the World Bank, the government said in its statement.
- Montengrin pensioners to receive 60 percent of their February pensions. Lowest pension stands at 523.8 dinars and highest 1.878 dinars.

- Peter Gumpel of Austrian Fajfazen Bank Group visited Montenegrin Agency for privatisation and said the group was interested in republic's voucher and cash privatisation. -- Belgrade Newsroom ++381 11 222 4254
